events.title: Rope Lab: Play & Connection - pain
events.description:
This is our experimental shibari playground for all skill levels. Each month explores a new topic — from shame and semenawa to performance, advanced movement, or the mythical “3rd rope” in TKs. We rotate between two themes, always bringing new inspiration to your rope practice. Open to all levels with foundational knowledge. Bring your curiosity, your questions, and your rope. 
This month we are focusing on: pain – weather you call it s/m or semenawa, this class is all about exploring how to use rope to create pain. We will explore both external pain and uncomfortable body positions. This class is suitable for all skill levels. 
Play & Connection
These classes are dedicated to the research of the interpersonal, connective, and fun side of shibari. Forget about rope technique for a while and learn hands-on skills for actually playing with what you know. The topic varies from month to month, and can be anything from pain and predicament ties to fun games like rope fight club. Come learn the skills that take your sessions from good to fantastic!

events.title: Maria Baptist Trio – Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests
events.description: Maria Baptist Trio Five Special Nights : Trio & Guests FEAT TODAY : Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius Maria Baptist gehört zu den profiliertesten Pianistinnen und Komponistinnen des zeitgenössischen Jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur nennt sie »eine der großen Jazzmusikerinnen aus Deutschland«, All About Jazz beschreibt ihren Klavierstil als » unendlich intelligent und stilvoll «. Sie wurde fünf Mal für den Preis der Deutschen Schallplattenkritik nominiert, darunter für Soloklavier-, Kammerjazz- und Jazzorchester-Produktionen. Ein zentraler Bezugspunkt ihrer Musik ist das Trio mit Fabian Timm am Bass und Heinz Lichius am Schlagzeug . Hier ist im kleinen Format das Großorchestrale ihres Werkkatalogs hörbar: Kompositionen fließen ineinander, formen suitenhafte Rahmen, weite Spannungsbögen wechseln zwischen Intimität und Kraft, Improvisationen durchziehen die Stücke und verweben sich mit dem Material. In der Reihe Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests spielt das Trio zunächst zwei Konzerte. Danach erweitert Maria Baptist die Besetzung jeweils an einem eigenen Abend mit Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger und Jan von Klewitz. — Maria Baptist is one of the most distinctive pianists and composers in contemporary jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur refers to her as “one of Germany’s greatest jazz musicians,” while All About Jazz describes her piano style as “ infinitely clever and classy .“ She has been nominated five times for the German Record Critics’ Award, including solo piano, chamber jazz, and jazz orchestra productions. A central focus of her music is the trio with Fabian Timm on bass and Heinz Lichius on drums . Here, the orchestral dimension of her music becomes audible in a small format: compositions flow into one another, forming suite-like structures; extended arcs of tension move between intimacy and power; improvisations run through the pieces and intertwine with the written material. As part of the series Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests, the trio opens with two concerts. Maria Baptist then expands the ensemble on separate evenings with Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger and Jan von Klewitz. events.title: Practical Reflections on Intentional Kink Space Facilitation
events.description:
As Kink Space Facilitators, we experience a wide range of impressions in our work. We plan juicy offers, trauma and queer inclusive, and hold space for experiences, uncertainties, fuck ups, desires and much more. After planning and implementation comes reflection and evaluation. The ‘how was I’ as a professional and personally. 
Alexander Hahne, gay trans man, trainer and speaker for trans-specific topics in the field of sexual health, sex educator, somatic counselor, sexuality focussed bodyworker, systemic sex therapist, dancer and pleasure activist. Leader of workshops and individual counseling on the topics of body awareness, intimacy and sexuality. He works in the field of sexuality for about 20 years with almost 15 years of facilitation in pleasure and kink spaces. With his work he directly support them in their own experience of the body as well as the possibility of uncovering and using access to their own pleasurable potential. 
What happens in the workshop?
In this workshop, we will first put on our oxygen masks and subject our work to a reality check to see how it actually was. 
For example, we will address the following questions: 

Which methods worked really well and why?
Did the planning of your trauma-informed process have the desired effect during implementation?
Were there situations in which you felt uncertain or overwhelmed? What did you do then? What could be different next time?
Which methods did you use and why? What worked, what didn’t and why?

Yes, there is always too little time and the physical space is different than expected… how do you deal with that? How does that affect your stress level and facilitation? 
The approach is to separate your behaviour from you as a person. You as a person are highly valued and your behaviour is criticised. 
Note
This offering connects to and extends Ceci Ferox’s workshops Intentional Kink Space Facilitation and Intentional Kink Spaces: Structures and Organizing. You can purchase the recordings in our shop. If you did not have the opportunity to be part of these classes, we are offering the recordings for you to purchase as well. The recordings will be available until July 16th, 2026. This is optional, not mandatory. If you were part of one or both of these workshops, you can email us and get free access to the recordings again, if you purchase a ticket to this class.

There is something extraordinarily powerful in feeling and playing with consensual and voluntary pain. Why would a person want to feel pain? Why would another love to give it to someone else? How is pain and the processing of it changed depending on the context and relation it is put into?

In short, this class will fry your brain with nerdy knowledge and allow you to think about your interest in pain play on a whole new level. Come for the facts, stay for the soul-searching of why sadomasochism is fucking delicious. 
What we will discuss

Define Pain?
Good pain, bad pain?
What do consent, trust and context have to do with it?
How to receive and process pain

Why the fuck are we doing this?

Playfight bringt kreative Ideen und ausgelassenes Spielen mit achtsamem Kämpfen in einer sicheren und respektvollen Umgebung zusammen. Wir kämpfen miteinander und nicht gegeneinander. Es geht uns ums Spaß haben und nicht ums besiegen. Wir setzen unsere Kräfte ein ohne verletzen zu wollen. Vorsichtig, spielerisch, kräftiger, ausgelassen, achtsam. Bei uns wird viel gelacht. Playfight macht Spaß – und manchmal sogar ein deutliches Glücksgefühl. Vorerfahrung im Kämpfen oder besondere sportliche Fitness ist nicht erforderlich. Faire MitspielerInnen sind uns herzlich willkommen. Wir nehmen aufeinander Rücksicht und begegnen einander mit Respekt und Neugierde. Es geht uns um Körperkontakt ohne sexuellen Kontext, um Bewegung und darum intensiven Spaß zu haben. Regeln Wir playfighten maximal in Kniehöhe, um die Fallhöhe gering zu halten Jede/r kann jederzeit STOP sagen oder 3 mal abklopfen. Die Situation wird damit sofort beendet. Das bedeutet nicht unbedingt, dass der Kampf ganz abgebrochen werden muss, sondern man kann auch kurz stoppen und die Lage klären. Ausdrücklich verboten sind Kampftechniken, deren Zweck es ist, zu verletzen, also KEIN Würgen, Treten, Schlagen, Hebeln, Beißen, festes Haare ziehen… Vor einem Kampf können Vorabspachen über spezielle Wünsche oder/und persönliche Empfindlichkeiten getroffen werden. Ihr könnt aber auch einfach schauen, welche Dynamik sich zwischen euch entwickelt, man kann sich auch während des Spielens weiter absprechen, und ansonsten kann man im Zweifelsfall ja jederzeit einfach „STOP“ sagen und die Situation klären. Ablauf Aufwärmen und Kurzworkshop • wir aktivieren unseren unseren Körper mit verschiedenen Übungen • üben praktisch ein, die eigenen Grenzen zu setzen und die des Grenzen des Partners zu respektieren • probieren verschiedene Ideen aus wie man kämpfen kann • machen ein kleine Roll- und Fallschule • und lernen uns dabei natürlich schon ein bisschen kennen Hauptteil Zum Kämpfen treffen sich 2 Personen in der Mitte des Kreises. KampfpartnerInnen können sich auf verschiedene Art finden. Wer aufgefordert wird und nicht möchte, sagt oder signalisiert einfach „Nein“, ohne dass das nein begründet werden muss. Die anderen TeilnehmerInnen bilden den Außenkreis und beobachten den Kampf und helfen dadurch einen sicheren Raum zu schaffen. events.description:
This is the Saturday single ticket event. For buying a full weekend ticket, go to the weekend event. 
Saturday gives you the tools that make shibari fun — or intense, or meditative, or horny, or whatever flavor of rope you want to create. Ceci will get you started with the most essential techniques: the lark’s head, the single column tie, clean wrapping, managing tension, and staying safe. Once those basics are in place, we spend the rest of the day putting them to use in playful, intuitive ways. 
We’ll explore freestyle tying and improvisation to loosen the pressure of “doing it right.” Through one-rope exercises, wrapping, unwrapping, and re-wrapping bodies, you’ll learn to follow curiosity instead of memorizing patterns. Because rope isn’t static — people move — we’ll also practice guiding and responding to movement through levers, spirals, and simple transitions like sitting to standing or shifting limbs mid-tie. 
Along the way, we dive into the emotional and psychological effects of rope: how body positions, pacing, tension, and proximity can shift headspace and shape intention. With just a few simple ties, you’ll learn to create sessions that feel impactful, intimate, and expressive.

Larkshead & single column tie

events.title: Rope Fundamentals: Shibari Starter Kit Weekend
events.description:
Kick off your rope journey with a weekend that bundles our entire Rope Fundamentals series into one playful, beginner-friendly shibari workshop. 
Across two days, you’ll move from the simplest building blocks to a clear understanding of how harnesses work. Whether you’re brand new, brushing off old skills, or craving a solid base before exploring deeper techniques, this weekend is designed to set you up with confidence, creativity, and connection. 
You can bring someone to tie with or come solo and find a partner at the workshop. 
Join us for the full journey, or pick the day that suits you best: 
Get Your Saturday (Foundations & Fun), only ticket here.
Get your Sunday (Nerdery & Harnesses), only ticket here. 
Foundations & Fun
Saturday gives you the tools that make shibari fun — or intense, or meditative, or horny, or whatever flavor of rope you want to create. Ceci will get you started with the most essential techniques: the lark’s head, the single column tie, clean wrapping, managing tension, and staying safe. Once those basics are in place, we spend the rest of the day putting them to use in playful, intuitive ways. 
We’ll explore freestyle tying and improvisation to loosen the pressure of “doing it right.” Through one-rope exercises, wrapping, unwrapping, and re-wrapping bodies, you’ll learn to follow curiosity instead of memorizing patterns. Because rope isn’t static — people move — we’ll also practice guiding and responding to movement through levers, spirals, and simple transitions like sitting to standing or shifting limbs mid-tie. 
Along the way, we dive into the emotional and psychological effects of rope: how body positions, pacing, tension, and proximity can shift headspace and shape intention. With just a few simple ties, you’ll learn to create sessions that feel impactful, intimate, and expressive. 
Take aways:

Larkshead & single column tie
Rope safety
One rope tying, wrapping & unwrapping
Playing with different intentions and moods
Moving bodies & tying in movement

Nerdery & Harnesses
Sunday is for the rope nerds (or for anyone ready to become one). Today we dive into the mechanics behind stable, comfortable, body-friendly tying. We’ll explore how to apply rope with intention, how to create structures that fit real bodies, and how to make your tying smoother, safer, and more efficient. 
You’ll learn counter tensions, ladder structures, your first frictions, and how to wrap with flow and consistency. These building blocks are what allow harnesses to hold their shape. We’ll also cover ergonomics and hand techniques, like hooking and pulling rope, so you can tie for longer without soreness or strain. 
With these tools in place, we’ll begin tying simple harnesses and, more importantly, understanding why they work. You’ll get a clear picture of the core components (anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, and cinches) and start recognizing the logic behind shibari structures. This modular thinking becomes the foundation for everything that comes after. 
Take aways:

Double column tie
Rope handling & ergonomics
Tension, counter tension & ladders
Intro to harnesses: anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, cinches
Frictions: Half hitch, full stop, munter hitch, in-line single column tie

Trumpeter Dima Bondarev’s lyrical intensity meets the harmonic imagination of pianist Kit Downes, grounded by the elastic groove and sensitivity of bassist Josh Ginsburg and drummer Marc Michel. Kit Downes is internationally acclaimed for his deeply expressive approach to piano and improvisation, working across jazz, contemporary classical, and experimental music. His collaborations span an extensive range of leading European improvisers and ensembles.
Josh Ginsburg is an in-demand bassist and improviser whose playing is noted for its warmth, flexibility, and strong melodic sensibility within adventurous contemporary jazz settings.
Marc Michel is recognized for his dynamic, highly interactive drumming and broad stylistic range, performing with many leading musicians on the European jazz scene.

events.title: Rope Fundamentals Weekend: Nerdery & Harnesses
events.description:
This is the Sunday single ticket event. For buying a full weekend ticket, go to the weekend event. 
Sunday is for the rope nerds (or for anyone ready to become one). Today we dive into the mechanics behind stable, comfortable, body-friendly tying. We’ll explore how to apply rope with intention, how to create structures that fit real bodies, and how to make your tying smoother, safer, and more efficient. 
You’ll learn counter tensions, ladder structures, your first frictions, and how to wrap with flow and consistency. These building blocks are what allow harnesses to hold their shape. We’ll also cover ergonomics and hand techniques, like hooking and pulling rope, so you can tie for longer without soreness or strain. 
With these tools in place, we’ll begin tying simple harnesses and, more importantly, understanding why they work. You’ll get a clear picture of the core components (anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, and cinches) and start recognizing the logic behind shibari structures. This modular thinking becomes the foundation for everything that comes after.

events.title: ERNST BIER NEW TRIO – «TRIPLE»
events.description: ERNST BIER NEW TRIO « TRIPLE » FEAT : Christian Müller-Tal Arditi Deutsch Triple ist ein neues Bandprojekt vom Schlagzeuger Ernst Bier, entstanden vor 5 Monaten im A-Trane. Im April spielten der Gitarrist Tal Arditi, der Bassist Christian Müller und Ernst Bier zum zweiten Mal im Little Shop of Jazz von Ernst miteinander. Die Chemie zwischen den Musikern stimmte sofort und das Publikum war sehr begeistert. Das veranlasste die Musiker dazu ein neues Trio zu gründen und hier sind sie noch einmal! Lassen Sie sich mitreißen von der ungeheuren Spiellaune dieser exzellenten Musiker. Sie leben mit und durch ihre Musik, eine Tatsache, die sie ausnahmslos mit viel Freude an die Zuhörer weitergeben . Tal Arditi ist ein israelischer, in Berlin lebender Jazz-Gitarrist und Komponist. Anerkannt als junges Gitarrenwunder, begann Tal im Alter von 16 Jahren mit dem Studium im prestigeträchtigen „Jazzinstitut“ – Programm der „Rimon Music University“. Im Alter von 18 Jahren schloss er auf der renommierten Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon in der Nähe von Tel Aviv erfolgreich mit einem Jazz-Diplom ab und beschloss nach Berlin zu ziehen. In Berlin wurde Tal Arditi schnell zu einem der gefragtesten Musiker in der internationalen und lokalen Jazzszene und begann, regelmäßig in Clubs in ganz Europa sowie auf Festivals wie dem Umbria Jazz-Festival, dem Xjazz Festival, dem Red Sea Festival, dem Fusion Festival oder dem Open Air Keintal zu spielen. Christian Müller ist Bassist und Komponist, der nach den Stationen Hamburg und Amsterdam, seit 2019 den Mittelpunkt seines Schaffens nach Berlin verlegt hat. Er studierte an der HfMT Hamburg sowie am Conservatorium van Amsterdam. Parallel dazu wurde er ins Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) unter der Leitung von Niels Klein und Jiggs Whigham aufgenommen. Konzertreisen führten ihn auf Bühnen in- und außerhalb Deutschlands. Unter anderem: Elbjazz-Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica-Festival(DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In der Vergangenheit spielte er mit: John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselmanm Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz und noch vielen weiteren fabelhaften Musikerinnen. Christians Arbeit als Sideman ist auf mehreren Alben mit diversen Projekten dokumentiert. Ende 2025 kam sein Debütalbum „Golden Gloom“ heraus, welches ausschließlich Eigenkompositionen enthält. Ernst Bier studierte Schlagzeug bei Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier und Elvin Jones. Von 1983-1987 lebte und arbeitete er in NY-City. Nach seiner Rückkehr aus den Staaten lebte Ernst zunächst bei Köln und dann ab 1992 in Berlin. Die Liste der Musiker, mit denen er gearbeitet hat, liest sich wie ein Who’s Who des Jazz. Mit seinem einfühlsamen Spiel, seiner Hingabe und seiner konstruktiven Art hat er sich zu einem hochgeschätzten und gefragten Schlagzeuger entwickelt. English Triple is a new band project by drummer Ernst Bier, formed two months ago at the A-Trane jazz club. In April, guitarist Tal Arditi, bassist Christian Müller, and Ernst Bier played together for the second time in Ernst’s Little Shop of Jazz. The chemistry between the three musicians clicked immediately, and the audience was thrilled. This prompted the musicians to form a new trio , and here they are again! Let yourself be swept away by the incredible energy of these excellent musicians. They live with and through their music, a passion they consistently share with their audience with great joy . Tal Arditi is an Israeli jazz guitarist and composer living in Berlin. Recognized as a young guitar prodigy, Tal began studying at the prestigious “Jazz Institute” program at Rimon Music University at the age of 16. At the age of 18, he successfully graduated with a jazz diploma from the renowned Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon near Tel Aviv and decided to move to Berlin. In Berlin, Tal Arditi quickly became one of the most sought-after musicians on the international and local jazz scene and began playing regularly in clubs throughout Europe as well as at festivals such as the Umbria Jazz Festival, the Xjazz Festival, the Red Sea Festival, the Fusion Festival, and the Open Air Keintal. Christian Müller is a bassist and composer who, after spending time in Hamburg and Amsterdam, moved his creative center to Berlin in 2019. He studied at the HfMT Hamburg and the Conservatorium van Amsterdam. At the same time, he was accepted into the Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) under the direction of Niels Klein and Jiggs Whigham. Concert tours have taken him to stages in Germany and abroad. Among others: Elbjazz Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica Festival (DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In the past, he has played with John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselman, Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz, and many other fabulous musicians. Christian’s work as a sideman is documented on several albums with various projects. At the end of 2025, his debut album “Golden Gloom” was released, which contains exclusively his own compositions. Ernst Bier studied percussion with Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier, and Elvin Jones. From 1983 to 1987, he lived and worked in New York City. After returning from the United States, Ernst first lived near Cologne and then, from 1992, in Berlin. The list of musicians he has worked with reads like a who’s who of jazz. events.description:
The singer Sophie Link views her voice not only as a melodic instrument, but continually explores its expressive potential at the intersection of improvisation, composition, and the spoken word.

The Tee.Trio is the working band of saxophonist Peter Ehwald. Born in Berlin, he has long been part of the local jazz scene and yet his work with musicians such as Tom Rainey, Robert Lanfermann and Laura Robles radiates beyond the borders of the City. The twins Andreas and Matthias Pichler play bass and drums with him. Matthias is highly virtuosic on bass and Andreas is theatrical and performative on drums.

For the three of them, the combination of jazz and modernity is part of his everyday music-making. Following their regular engagement at Berlin's Tee.Salon:iki, their release “Live in Berlin” will appear in the spring – a concert recording from the B-Flat jazz club. The Tee.Trio's concerts develop an improvisational pull in which anything is possible thanks to their irrepressible joy of playing—jazz tradition, heartbreaking ballads, folklore from Tyrol, and a sky-high search for freedom.

events.title: Aftercare Tools: Exploring Our Routes to Safety
events.description:
Aftercare isn’t just a nice idea — it’s a vital part of returning to homeostasis after intense scenes and powerful experiences. Through discussion and embodied exercises inspired by Jake Ernst’s “Routes of Safety,” we’ll explore tools for shared, self, and group aftercare, so that soft landings become as intentional as our scenes. 
What we will explore:

Who needs aftercare, what agreements are in place, and when care begins and ends
How consent, communication, and power dynamics shape aftercare from scene to scene and person to person
How to name our needs with honesty and compassion, especially when our capacity doesn’t match our partner’s
The often-overlooked realms of pre-care and during-care
Pathways for grounding, reconnection, and gentle reintegration

events.description:
Let’s slow down queerdos, and feel ourselves & our bodies in all our multidimensional glory. 
Little Purrrverts – Slow Pleasure Fest is a three-day gathering that is all about queer people coming together to slow down and feel themselves and their bodies in all their multidimensional glory. Highly skilled facilitators will offer a myriad of workshops and open spaces to enjoy learning and experiencing the pleasures of gender, sexuality, embodiment, kink, bodywork, and breathwork in a slow, intentional, and sensual manner. 
Join us and feel yourself and others while hanging out in our new space. We have multiple rooms and a huge 100 sqm garden at our disposal to just be luscious, slow, and sensual. Purrr! 
Program
Here is this year’s program. 
Details
-3-day fest, over 20 facilitated spaces/workshops, spaces to do bodywork, cuddles, be sensual or just hang out
-multiple rooms,  a dedicated space for introverts and people with neurodivergence to retreat, hang out spaces, kitchen, bathrooms, a garden, Berlin in the summer
-LGBTQIA+ people, only

-kink, sexuality, gender, sensuality, consent, bodywork, breathwork, sound work, touch, play, food nom nom
-we take it sloooooow, there is lots of space to just chill
-we have limited space for people to sleep over for a small extra fee (please book accommodation IMMEDIATELY, we cannot take request for it after booking)
-we offer breakfast, lunch, and snacks all day for a small extra fee (perfect if you don’t want to leave the bubble and just be luscious all day)
-free water, tea, ice for everyone, there might be cookies and popsicles
-we aim to make the space accessible for all kinds of bodies, the house is wheelchair accessible for the most part, if you need other accommodation, please let us know and we will make it happen

events.description:

Day @ c-base

Let’s DID it! @c-base – diesmal mit Linux & Sommerfest der BELUG

Am ersten Sonntag des Monats auf die gute Seite wechseln!

Im Juli wird es besonders: Der Digital Independence Day findet gemeinsam mit dem Sommerfest der BELUG – Berlin Linux User Group statt. Das heißt: digitale Selbstbestimmung, Linux, Austausch, Vorträge, Grillen und gute Gespräche an einem Ort.

Wir unterstützen dich dabei, deine digitale Autonomie zurückzugewinnen. Gemeinsam und Schritt für Schritt. Ob von X zu Mastodon, von Google Chrome zu Firefox oder von Windows zu Linux – wir helfen dir beim Wechsel!

Du möchtest Linux ausprobieren, Fragen stellen oder wissen, ob dein Gerät dafür geeignet ist? Du möchtest mehr über freie Software, Datenschutz oder digitale Alternativen erfahren, die unsere Demokratie stärken statt sie zu zerstören? Dann komm vorbei.

Dann lass uns zusammen loslegen!

Am

Sonntag, 05. Juli 2026

von 14 bis 18 Uhr

freuen wir uns auf dich in der

c-base

Rungestraße 20, 10179 Berlin

Es gibt Tee, Kaffee, Snacks, natürlich Cookies – und diesmal auch Sommerfest-Stimmung mit der BELUG. Fürs gemeinsame Grillen freuen wir uns, wenn du einen Salat, Brot, Aufstrich oder etwas anderes Leckeres fürs Buffet mitbringst.

Lasst uns gemeinsam Linux entdecken, digitale Alternativen ausprobieren und etwas für unsere digitale Unabhängigkeit tun!

Kostenlos, auch ohne Vorkenntnisse. Bring gern deine Endgeräte mit.

Der Zugang und der Raum sind barrierefrei.

Wieder mit dabei sind als Gastgeber der Hackspace c-base, das Projekt Digital-Zebra (VÖBB), Topio, der kleindatenverein, Anoxinon e.V., Computertruhe e.V. und der Möckernkiez e.V. Diesmal freuen wir uns außerdem besonders über die Zusammenarbeit mit der BELUG.

Schaut aber auch gerne bei der Veranstaltung vom Chaos Computer Club Berlin e.V. und dem xHain hack+makespace vorbei.

Gemeinsam mehr erreichen

Diese Veranstaltung ist Teil eines Netzwerks aus mehreren Organisationen und Initiativen in Berlin. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig mit Kompetenz, Erfahrung und praktischer Hilfe. Uns alle eint der Wunsch, Wissen zu teilen, voneinander zu lernen und solidarisch zusammenzuarbeiten.

Der DIDay bildet dabei den gemeinsamen Rahmen, in dem wir uns für digitale Selbstbestimmung und nachhaltige digitale Strukturen einsetzen.

Schau deshalb gern auch bei den Veranstaltungen der anderen beteiligten Organisationen vorbei. So entsteht ein vielfältiges Angebot, das Austausch, Vernetzung und gegenseitige Unterstützung lebendig macht.

I am pleased to present a new edition of Domingo Fantástico, a music and variety show series held at Donau115. Inspired by the great weekend television shows that shaped generations across Latin America and Spain, this event celebrates the diversity and creativity of the Spanish-speaking community in Berlin.

In this edition, we will travel through Mexico with three musical projects that, from different perspectives and artistic paths, keep alive the connection between tradition, identity, and contemporary creation.

The evening will feature Frieda, a singer, songwriter, and producer from Mexico City whose music embodies the spirit of neo-Mexicanity, bringing together Mexican folklore and contemporary songwriting. In an intimate acoustic format, she will present songs that connect Mexico and Europe through stories, emotions, and memory.

We will also welcome Sauceedo, a musician from Monterrey, for whom creating music is a way to experience flow and peace of mind, sharing songs born from a sincere and personal artistic journey.

Completing the line-up is El Cuervo del Norte from Guadalajara, presenting a repertoire of regional Mexican music inspired by the tradition of the corrido, where popular stories, legends, and reflections on life and death come together.

An evening dedicated to the richness and diversity of Mexican music, celebrating its roots and its presence within Berlin’s cultural scene.

events.title: Ben Osborn
events.description:
Ben Osborn presents a new set of songs and instrumentals for piano, electronics and voice, moving between fragile folk song, analogue electronic textures and contemporary classical composition. Drawing on both the deeply personal and the fiercely political, his music creates a space for tenderness, grief, hope and resistance.

Originally from Oxford and now based in Berlin, Osborn works across songwriting, composition and sound design. His 2022 release Studies on Nonostar Records explored the emotional reality of living through overlapping global crises, created as a multimedia project in collaboration with fine artist Andrea Huyoff.

His debut album Letters from the Border (2019) received widespread critical acclaim, described by the BBC as featuring “incredible orchestration, incredible words, a touch of Leonard Cohen and a touch of Björk.” The album was named one of the top 10 releases of 2019 by CurveBall Radio, while its title track was nominated for an International Songwriting Award. His music and collaborations have also appeared on Neue Meister, Deek Recordings, Delphian Records, Hot Topic and Cuculi Records, and his lyrics and poems have been published by Moot Press.

events.description:
Bio:
Alden Hellmuth is a saxophonist, composer, and improviser based in New York City. A graduate of the Herbie Hancock Institute, she received the 2025 German Jazz Prize for Debut Album of the Year (International) for her album Good Intentions (Fresh Sound Records) and has performed internationally at major venues and festivals including the NYC Winter Jazz Festival, Hollywood Bowl and Blue Note Jazz Festival, International Jazz Day (Morocco and Abu Dhabi), The Jazz Gallery, and Blue Note NYC. Alden has been recognized with numerous honors, including New Music USA’s Next Jazz Legacy (2026), Chamber Music America’s Performance Plus Grant (2025), ASCAP’s Herb Alpert Young Jazz Composer Award (2024), and the Focusyear Fellowship (2021-22). As an artist, Alden seeks expression through freedom, intuition, and a deep commitment to her craft. 

She'll be presenting music from her newest project, Tether, set to be released June 26th with Berlin-based record label Leiter Verlag, with NYC band Yvonne Rogers on piano, Timothy Angulo on drums, and Phil Donkin on bass.

Another Tether:
Alden Hellmuth’s Tether is a quartet that leans hard into density, motion, and low-end gravity. Developed during her time in Los Angeles, the project explores a striking array of moods, tones, and textures with intensity and unmistakable momentum. With her "challenging and evocative" (Jazz Times) compositional vision and a sharp improvisational language, Hellmuth has carefully and creatively crafted a new sonic realm using the distinct voices in her band. The recorded work, Hellmuth's sophomore release, features Los Angeles bassists Logan Kane and Miller Wrenn, acclaimed drummer Justin Brown, and appearances by pianist Paul Cornish and trumpeter Yakiv Tsvietinskyi. Out June 26th on Berlin-based label Leiter, Tether is a bold statement of intent.

DEUTSCH: Diese Woche präsentiert die gefeierte Jazzsängerin und Pädagogin Judy Niemack im A-Trane Singing Miles – eine besondere vokale Hommage an die Musik des legendären Trompeters Miles Davis . EN
This year’s Focusyear Band takes shape as a quintet of five strongly individual young musicians, each
bringing distinct backgrounds and influences into a shared artistic space. Their diversity generates a rich spectrum of musical colors and possibilities. What unites them is a deep engagement with both traditional and contemporary expressions of jazz and jazz-related music, and a strong commitment to the art of improvisation.

Swiss vocalist Alice Auclair combines a finely nuanced approach to song interpretation with harmonically informed improvisation, marked by a clear, magnetic voice and impressive intonation. Belgian guitarist Eliott Knuets stands out for his remarkable virtuosity and expressive range, revealing a musical maturity and rhythmic connectedness well beyond his years.

Australian pianist Wilbur Whitta brings exceptional rhythmic focus and architectural clarity, shaping solos that rise into moments of intensity and drive. Spanish bassist Eva Serrano forms the rhythmic and sonic foundation of the band with her pulse-oriented, resonant bass playing, while also expanding the ensemble’s texture through the use of her voice. 

Drummer Dae Bryant anchors and propels the group with a dynamic, soulful, and often poetic approach, continuously inventing new layers of accompaniment while responding in the moment to the sound of his fellow musicians.

During their year in Basel, these five musicians—selected from a large international pool of applicants—have taken part in an intensive program of coaching and performance. They have worked closely with an impressive group of internationally renowned jazz artists, including Allison Miller, Django Bates, Guillermo Klein, Ingrid Jensen, Ingrid Laubrock, Wolfgang Muthspiel, Kendrick Scott, Kris Davis, Lionel Loueke, Miguel Zenón, Jaleel Shaw, Michael Mayo, Mario Rom, Darcy James Argue, Linda May Han Oh, and Jonathan Blake. is collective in spirit, interactive in form, and marked by intensity, openness, and a distinctly
contemporary voice.

events.title: Mads Riis Quartet
events.description:
Rooted in jazz, our music weaves a tapestry of powerful, evocative melodies, ambient soundscapes, and minimalist aesthetics. It is an exploration of identity and belonging. At its core, the music stems from a longing to find one’s roots and a sense of grounding in a time marked by increasing uncertainty. The result is music that paints vivid portraits of the inner life, where nostalgia and hope converge. It often draws from places, memories, or relationships, hoping that the music will appeal to the listener, allowing them to relate and explore memories and emotions in their own way.

Mads Riis released his debut album in May 2026 on all streaming platforms - he was awarded the Karl Hofer Jazz-Stipendium in late-2025 for his compositions, where the jury stated: ”With his warm sound aesthetic and deeply emotional playing, Mads Riis impressed across the board. (…) As a composer and guitarist, he creates an intimate yet powerful musical language that impressively combines personal experiences and artistic maturity." 

He also won the first place in the Keep An Eye International Jazz Award final at BIMHUIS in april 2026 - playing his compositions with his group. This special perfomance will feature brand new songs and songs from the album.

Since 1995 I played here about 900 wonderful & surprising improvised happenings in music with lots of friends like Jay Clayton, Hayden Chisholm, Dave Douglas, Walter Norris, Mark Murphy, Till Brönner, Sebastian Merk, Andreas Edelmann, Jan Roder, Connie Crothers, Max Andrzejewski, Andy Fite etc.. Schmidt is a fine pianist, the salient features of his playing located somewhere between the Paul Bley of the mid-’60s and the Chick Corea of «Now He Sings, Now He Sobs». You might get an idea of his approach if I say that his first album was made (in 1995) with Lee Konitz, and a later one comprised a duo with Gary Peacock. events.title: Nils Kugelmann – «Where Nights Unfold» – Celebrating 5 Years Of The Trio
events.description: A Summer Residency Nils Kugelmann «Where Nights Unfold» Celebrating 5 Years Of The Trio Deutsch Fünf Abende. Gleicher Club, gleiche Band – anderes Ergebnis. In seiner Residency im A-Trane bringt Nils Kugelmann neue Kompositionen genau dorthin, wo sie hingehören: auf die Bühne – wo sie für diesen Moment ihre endgültige Form finden . Nils Kugelmann , geboren in München und heute in Berlin lebend, hat in erstaunlich kurzer Zeit einen klaren künstlerischen Eindruck hinterlassen. Direkt nach seinem Masterabschluss erschien sein Debüt Stormy Beauty (ACT) im Trio: Preise, ausverkaufte Konzerte, viel Aufmerksamkeit. Die Süddeutsche Zeitung sprach vom „ Bass-Berserker “, BR-Klassik vom „ Mega-Talent “. Mit dem zweiten Trio-Album Life Score (ACT) wurde daraus mehr als ein Versprechen – nämlich eine Handschrift. Seither ist einiges passiert: Konzerte mit dem Trio in ganz Europa und darüber hinaus – von Italien, der Schweiz und Österreich bis nach England, Rumänien, Kosovo und Ecuador. Zuletzt war die Band im legendären Ronnie Scott’s Jazz Club in London zu Gast. Parallel dazu zeigt Kugelmann weitere Facetten seines Spiels, etwa im Duo mit der Rising-star-Pianistin Shuteen Erdenebaatar auf dem aktuellen Album Under the Same Stars, das eine ruhigere, kammermusikalische Seite seiner Musik hörbar macht. In dieser Woche treffen neue Kompositionen auf ein Trio, das in den letzten fünf Jahren eng zusammengewachsen ist und gelernt hat, Risiko als Teil seines Sounds zu begreifen. Groove ist nicht nur eine Option, sondern ein Grundzustand . Und wenn etwas kippt, dann meist genau dorthin, wo es spannend wird. Was auffällt : Für Kugelmann hat der Kontrabass keine Nebenrolle, sondern eine erzählende Stimme im Zentrum seiner Musik. Seine Stücke bleiben in Bewegung und schlagen dabei immer wieder unerwartete Wege ein . Wer an einem Abend kommt, hört ein Konzert. Wer an mehreren kommt, hört eine Entwicklung . Und ja : Es wird Momente geben, die genau so nie wieder passieren . English Five nights. Same club, same band – different result. In his residency at A-Trane, Nils Kugelmann brings new compositions to the stage exactly where they belong: on the bandstand – where they find their final form in this moment . Born in Munich and now based in Berlin, Nils Kugelmann has made a clear artistic mark in a remarkably short time. Right after completing his master’s degree, he released his debut Stormy Beauty (ACT): awards, sold-out concerts, and wide attention followed. Süddeutsche Zeitung called him a “ bass berserker ”, BR-Klassik a “ mega talent ”. With his second album Life Score (ACT), this promise turned into a recognisable artistic voice. Since then, a lot has happened: concerts with the trio across Europe and beyond – from Italy, Switzerland and Austria to England, Romania, Kosovo and Ecuador. Most recently, the band appeared at the legendary Ronnie Scott’s Jazz Club in London. At the same time, Kugelmann explores other facets of his playing, for example in a duo with rising-star pianist Shuteen Erdenebaatar on the recent album Under the Same Stars, revealing a more intimate, chamber-music-like side of his artistry. This week, new compositions meet a trio that has grown closely together over the last five years and learned to embrace risk as part of its sound. Groove is not just an option, but a constant . And when things shift, it’s usually exactly where it gets interesting. What stands out : for Kugelmann, the double bass is not a supporting role, but a narrative voice at the centre of his music. His pieces stay in motion, constantly evolving and taking unexpected turns . One night is a concert. Several nights become an evolution . And yes : there will be moments that will never happen in quite the same way again . Nils Kugelmann — Bass, Composition Luca Zambito — Piano Sebastian Wolfgruber — Drums Fotos©Uli Neumann Cosel

events.description:
1st Part: QUIQUE SINESI SOLO
Quique Sinesi is a guitarrist and composer from Argentina,Winner of a Latin Grammy awards and recently nominated for Argentina's Gardel Awards for Best Instrumental Album,in his Solo Conert he will use different guitars 7 & 10 Strings etc,and will play his own compositions that utilize Argentine and Rio de la Plata sounds with the incorporation of improvisation

2nd Part: SINESIS BAND
Sinesis Project (Duo & Band), comprised of Quique and Augusto Sinesi (father and son), was formed in 2018. Their music is a captivating blend of Latin American, Rioplatense, and jazz styles, built on their original compositions. The duo has performed extensively in Argentina, toured Germany, and participated in prestigious events such as the "Guitarras del Mundo Festival" in Argentina. They also performed a live-recorded concert for "El Taller Latino" in New York City for its 42nd anniversary and gave a virtual presentation for "Music of Americas."

Their debut album, "Hojas y Rutas Nuevas," featuring Carlos "Negro" Aguirre and Joana Queiroz, was recorded in 2020 and released by Impartmaint Music in Japan in 2022. Currently, Sinesís Project is actively performing across the European music scene.
on this occasion ,they will be performing with two incredible musicians from Brazilwith extensive international experience: Thiago Duarte :Double Bass and Amoy Rivas percussion
